questions.history: Request application/jsonl for the two-message Flux.
questions.prediction: The PR reports canEncode false on the parent despite advertised streaming support. The landing should return true and emit two LF-terminated lines decoding to first and second in order with the compact printer.
questions.basis: The downstream receiver treats one physical line as one complete JSON value. The regression compares the two compact messages including their LF terminators.
questions.refutation: Selection fails, an array or extra line appears, or parsing either line gives the wrong message.

questions.history: Select application/x-ndjson for the same messages and compact printer.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should accept the type and yield the same two ordered records.
questions.basis: The earlier NDJSON support and the existing two-message streaming regression establish this format.
questions.refutation: Selection or line-by-line readback differs at either revision.

questions.history: At the landing keep the nested messages and JSONL type fixed but use new ProtobufJsonEncoder() with its default printer.
questions.prediction: A JSON Lines reader still expects exactly two independently parseable records. The default constructor uses JsonFormat.printer() without the test’s compacting option, so interior formatting newlines may break that contract.
questions.basis: Formatting whitespace is allowed within ordinary JSON but a physical LF delimits a record here. Parsing whole DataBuffers would hide this distinction.
questions.refutation: A third nonempty line, a line that cannot parse by itself, or loss of either message refutes default JSONL framing.
